section_summary.extract_value: This introduction summarizes the development and revision of the Body Appreciation Scale (BAS) and the newer BAS-2, noting the BAS's original components and the BAS-2's 10-item one-dimensional structure. It highlights cross-cultural issues with the BAS (reporting that some items failed to load in samples from multiple countries) and states that Tylka and Wood-Barcalow (2015b) confirmed the BAS-2's factor structure across three studies in U.S. adults. section_summary.evidence_source: Scholars are shifting from a focus on body image disturbances to a comprehensive account of the body image concept that includes positive body image (Tylka & Wood-Barcalow, 2015a). This revised measure, the BAS-2, consists of 10 items, five of which were retained from the parent scale and five of which are newly devised. Across three studies with adults from the United States, Tylka and Wood-Barcalow (2015b) confirmed the BAS-2's one-dimensional factor structure, which was invariant across participant sex.
